label: eq:entropy-M-bound
title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to prove the lemma for $0\leq \theta < 1$; the endpoint $\theta=1$ follows from continuity.
Apply the relative entropy variational formula with
\[
    f_\theta(x,y)
      :=\frac{t\,(2\theta xy-\theta^2(x^2+y^2))}{1-\theta^2},
\] where (recall) $t=1/(2\sigma(r)^2)$.
We immediately see that the expectation of $f_\theta$ under $\mu^{(2)}_{r,r,\theta}$ is zero. On the other hand, we compute
\[\mathbb{E}_{\mu_r\otimes\mu_r\unskip\space}\left[e^{f_\theta}\right]=\frac1{Z_r^2}\sum_{x,y\ne0}
        \exp\left(-\frac{t\,(x^2+y^2-2\theta xy)}
                           {1-\theta^2}\right)=:M_r(\theta).
\]
The relative entropy variational formula then gives 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:entropy-M-bound}
    D_r(\theta)\ge-\log M_r(\theta).
\end{equation}

For $r \geq 1.2$, we have $t\le t(1.2)<.63$. Then,
\[
    Z_r = \sum_{m\in \mathbb{Z} \setminus\{0\}} e^{-t m^2} \ge2(e^{-.63}+e^{-.63 \cdot 4})>1.1,
\]
which proves that $0<c_r<1$.

For ease of notation, let $s:=\sqrt{1-\theta^2}$ and $c:=\pi^2/t$, and define the two series 
\[
    \mathcal S(u) :=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}e^{-um^2}, \qquad \mathcal A(\theta) :=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-c(m^2+2\theta mn+n^2)},
\]
noting that $Z_r = \mathcal S(t)-1$.
Poisson summation gives 
\begin{align}
    Z_r&=\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}\,\mathcal S\left(\frac{\pi^2}{t}\right)-1,\label{eq:Z-Poisson}\\
    Z_r^2M_r(\theta)
      &=\frac{\pi}{t}s\mathcal A(\theta)-2\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}\,s\, \mathcal S\left(\frac{\pi^2}{t}s^2\right)+1,
      \label{eq:M-Poisson}
\end{align}
We now claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound}
    Z_r^2M_r(\theta)
       \le sZ_r^2+1.1(1-s)Z_r.
\end{equation}
The proof only uses estimates of positive theta series. If $s\ge.98$, then note that combining \eqref{eq:Z-Poisson} and \eqref{eq:M-Poisson} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Zr-bashing}Z_r^2 M_r(\theta) - sZ_r^2 = \frac{\pi}{t} s(\mathcal A(\theta) - \mathcal A(0)) - 2\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}\,s\left(\mathcal S\left(\frac{\pi^2}{t}s^2\right)-\mathcal S\left(\frac{\pi^2}{t}\right)\right)+(1-s).\end{equation}
Pairing $(m,n)$ with $(m,-n)$ gives
\[
    \mathcal A(\theta)-\mathcal A(0)
       \le\frac{2\pi^4}{t^2}\theta^2
          \left(\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}m^2e^{-\pi^2(1-\theta)m^2/t}\right)^2.
\]
The first term in the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:Zr-bashing} is thus at most
$2.4\cdot10^{-7}(1-s)$. The second term there (involving $\mathcal S$) is nonpositive since $s \leq 1$ and $\mathcal S(u)$ is decreasing in $u$. Since $Z_r \geq 1.1$, the entire right-hand side of \eqref{eq:Zr-bashing} is at most $(2.4\cdot 10^{-7} + 1)(1-s) \leq 1.1 (1-s)Z_r$. This proves \eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound} in this case.

Suppose next that $s<.98$, and for ease of notation, set $v=t/s^2$. Isolating the diagonal
$m+n=0$ in $\mathcal A(\theta)$, we change variables to $m+n,m-n$, using that $m^2 + 2\theta mn + n^2 = (1+\theta)(m+n)^2/2 + (1-\theta)(m-n)^2/2.$ Applying \eqref{eq:theta-sum-elementary}, separate the common leading contribution $1+\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{v}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}-2\right)$. After this contribution is removed from both sides of \eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound}, it suffices to show that the remaining diagonal, off-diagonal, and Poisson-correction errors have total size at most $(1-s)\left(\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}-2\right)$, which is a positive quantity since $t < \pi/4$. Normalizing the three error terms by this quantity gives, respectively:
\begin{align*}
 E_d(v,s)
   &:=\frac{\sqrt{\pi/v}\,\eta(\pi^2/v)}{1-s},\\
 E_o(v,s)
   &:=\frac{\sqrt{\pi/v}\,\eta\left(\frac{\pi^2(1+\theta)}{2vs^2}\right)\left(1+\eta\left(\frac{\pi^2}{2v(1+\theta)}\right)\right)}
   {(1-s)(1-2s\sqrt{v/\pi})},\\
 E_c(v,s)
   &:=\frac{2s\,\eta(\pi^2/(vs^2))}
   {(1-s)(1-2s\sqrt{v/\pi})},
\end{align*}
where $\eta(u):=2e^{-u}/(1-e^{-3u})$.
The inequality $E_d+E_o+E_c<1$ is then a sufficient condition for
\eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound}.
Interval
evaluation gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
v\text{-range}&E_d&E_o&E_c&\text{total}\\ \hline
(0,1]&<.0009&<.1756&<.00030&<.177\\
{[1,30]}&<.8684&<.0007&<.00003&<.870.
\end{array}
\]
The bounds are uniform for
$0<s\le\min\{.98,\sqrt{.63/v}\}$, including the limiting boundaries,
and prove \eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound} for $v\le30$.
These are direct interval evaluations of the explicit theta sums, under the
conventions described in \cref{app:numer-conventions}.

Finally, if $v\ge30$, the terms $x=y$ in the original sum defining
$M_r(\theta)$ contribute at most $Z_r$. Then, 
\eqref{eq:theta-sum-elementary} bounds all other terms by
\[
    \left(\mathcal S(v(1+\theta)/2)-1\right)\mathcal S(v(1-\theta)/2)
       <1.3\cdot10^{-6}\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{t}}\right)<.1(1-s)Z_r.
\]
Since $s<\sqrt{.63/30}$, this again gives
\eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation-theta-bound}. Consequently,
\[
    M_r(\theta)
       \le s+\frac{1.1(1-s)}{Z_r}
       =c_r+(1-c_r)s.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:entropy-M-bound}, this proves the first inequality
in \eqref{eq:entropy-interpolation}.  The second follows from
$-\log(1-x)\ge x$ and
$1-\sqrt{1-\theta^2}\ge\theta^2/2$.

label: eq:small-window-E
title: Proof
body_md:
Define $f(u)=u/(e^u-1).$
The left-hand side of
\eqref{eq:small-window-main-scalar} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:small-window-E}
    \mathcal E(r,K)
       :=Z_r^2(1-q(r)d(K))f\left(\frac{-\log p(K)}{d(K)^2}\right).
\end{equation}
The remainder of the proof uses only positive one-dimensional series. We have
\[
    \frac1{d(K)}=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{K^{2j}}{(2j+1)!!},
    \qquad
    p(K)=\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\,Ke^{-K^2/2}
          \sum_{j\ge0}\frac{K^{2j}}{(2j+1)!!},
\]
while Poisson summation gives
\[
    q(r)=1+\frac{1-2\pi^{5/2}/t^{3/2}\cdot \mathcal T_2(\pi^2/t)}{Z_r}<1+\frac1{Z_r},
    \qquad
    Z_r>\sqrt{2\pi}\,r-1.54
\]
for $r\ge5$. For $r\geq 80$ we may improve the second inequality above by replacing $1.54$ with $1.502$.


These identities also show that, for fixed $r$, both factors in
\eqref{eq:small-window-E} are increasing in $K$ on the feasible
subinterval $K\le1$.
On this subinterval, the map
\[
    K\longmapsto
    \frac{q(r)}{d(K)}-1-\frac1{r^2K^2}
\]
is strictly increasing, tends to $-\infty$ as $K\downarrow0$, and is
positive at $K=1$. Let $k_0(r)$ be its unique zero,
and define $K_0(r)=\max\{10/r,k_0(r)\}$. It is therefore enough to
evaluate $\mathcal E(r,K)$ at $K=K_0(r)$. The series above, with
geometric bounds on their positive tails, give the following outward-rounded
lower bounds:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{range}&\mathcal E(r,K)\\ \hline
1\le K\le2&>16\\
K=10/r,\ 10\le r\le80&>1.93\\
K=10/r,\ 80\le r\le81.5&>1.02\\
K=k_0(r),\ r\ge81.4&>1.044.
\end{array}
\]
The last two ranges overlap because bisection in the two monotone defining
equations shows that the change of branch occurs in $81.4<r<81.5$.
For the unbounded last range, the substitution $x=1/r$, together with
the Poisson representations above, extends the defining expressions
continuously to $x=0$; interval evaluation on
$x\in [0,1/81.4]$ gives the  bound in the last entry of the table.
This proves \eqref{eq:small-window-main-scalar}, and in particular
$q(r)d(K)<1$.

For the second estimate, the same positive-series bounds give
\[
    s_0\ge .46K\quad(K\le1),\qquad
    s_0\ge .4\quad(1\le K\le2),
\]
and hence
\[
    u_0>1.5r^2\quad(K\ge1),\qquad
    u_0>1.91r^2K^2\ge191\quad(K\le1).
\]
Since $r\geq 5$ we have $q(r) > 1$, so $\pi^5/t^3<8\pi^5r^6$. Furthermore, by comparing consecutive terms, we obtain $\mathcal T_2(u)\le2e^{-u}/(1-4e^{-3u}),$
and checking the endpoints of the same four monotone ranges yields
\eqref{eq:small-window-remainder-bound}.

label: eq:small-window-M-chord
title: Proof
body_md:
First, we note that \cref{lem:small-window-scalar} immediately gives $0<q(r)d(K)<1$.  Now, using the Poisson formula
\eqref{eq:M-Poisson} only for $s\ge s_0$, we claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:small-window-M-chord}
    M_r(\theta)\le s+C_{r,K}(1-s),
\end{equation}
where $M_r(\theta)$ was defined in \cref{app:entropy-interpolation} and 
\[
    C_{r,K}
       :=\frac{1+4\pi^5/t^3 \cdot \mathcal T_2(u_0)^2}{Z_r^2}.
\]
Indeed, subtracting $s$ times the identity at $\theta=0$ in
\eqref{eq:M-Poisson} and pairing the summands indexed by
$(m,n)$ and $(m,-n)$ gives
\[
    \mathcal A(\theta)-\mathcal A(0)
       \le\frac{2\pi^4}{t^2}\theta^2
          \left(\sum_{m\in\mathbb{Z}}
            m^2e^{-\frac{\pi^2}{t}(1-\theta)m^2}\right)^2.
\]
Also, we have $\mathcal S(\pi^2 s^2 / t)\ge \mathcal S(\pi^2/t)$, so the contribution by terms involving $\mathcal S$ to the difference between
the proposed upper bound and $M_r(\theta)$ is nonnegative.
Finally,
\[
    \theta^2\le2(1-s),
    \qquad
    \frac{\pi^2}{t}(1-\theta)\ge
       \frac{\pi^2}{t}\left(1-\sqrt{1-s_0^2}\right)=u_0.
\]
These inequalities prove \eqref{eq:small-window-M-chord}.

Since $0<q(r)d(K)<1$, the function
\[
    g(s):=\frac{s^{q(r)d(K)}-s}{1-s}
\]
is increasing on $s\in(0,1)$, and
\[
    g(s_0)
      \ge(1-q(r)d(K))
        \frac{s_0\log(1/s_0)}{1-s_0}.
\]
Thus \cref{lem:small-window-scalar} implies that $C_{r,K}<g(s_0)\le g(s)$ for $s\ge s_0$.
From \eqref{eq:entropy-M-bound} and
\eqref{eq:small-window-M-chord}, we obtain
\[
    D_r(\theta)>-q(r)d(K)\log s.
\]
On the other hand, \eqref{eq:Gaussian-small-window} gives
\[
    \frac{q(r)}{d(K)}G_K(\theta)
       \le-q(r)d(K)\log s.
\]
Combining these yields \eqref{eq:small-window-profile} for $s\ge s_0$.

For $s\le s_0$, the entropy
$H(\mu^{(2)}_{r,r,\theta})$ is even and concave (\cref{prop:F2 entropy derivatives}), so $D_r(\theta)$
is increasing on $0\le\theta\le1$.  Also
\[
    G_K(\theta)\le G_K(1)=-\log p(K),
\]
and
\[
    \frac{q(r)}{d(K)}(-\log p(K))
       =-q(r)d(K)\log s_0.
\]
The strict inequality already proved at $s=s_0$ therefore covers the
remaining interval.

title: Proof
body_md:
For any $0\le u\le1/4$, the relative entropy variational formula gives
\[
    D_r(\theta)
      \ge u\theta-\log\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[e^{uXY/r^2}\right],
\]
where $X,Y$ are independent with law $\mu_r$.  By symmetry, the
exponential inside the expectation may be replaced by its hyperbolic
cosine.  Using the easy bounds
\[
    \cosh z\le1+\frac{z^2}{2}e^{|z|}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    2|XY|\le X^2+Y^2,
\]
we obtain
\[
    \mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[e^{uXY/r^2}\right]
      \le1+\frac{u^2}{2}
       \left(\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[X^2e^{uX^2/(2r^2)}\right]}{r^2}\right)^2.
\]
Recalling the notation $\mathcal T_2(v)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}j^2e^{-vj^2},$
the ratio in parentheses is $\mathcal T_2(t-u/(2r^2))/\mathcal T_2(t).$
This ratio decreases with $t$ and increases with $u/(2r^2)$.  Since $t\ge t(1.2)>.627$ and $0\le u/(2r^2)\le\frac18$,
it suffices to evaluate
\[
    \frac{\mathcal T_2(.627-1/8)}{\mathcal T_2(.627)}<1.45.
\]
Five terms followed by an integral bound for the positive tail certify this inequality.  It follows that
\[
    \log\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[e^{uXY/r^2}\right]\le2u^2.
\]
Taking $u=\theta/4$ proves
\eqref{eq:near-binary-entropy-bound}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\alpha=q(r)/d(K)$, and write
$F_2(\theta)=F_2(rK,\alpha,r,r,\theta)$. Since $rK\ge10$ and
$r\le1.2$, we have $K\ge25/3$.

Suppose first that $q(r)\le8$.  Using
\eqref{eq:Gaussian-Hermite-coarse}, $1-p(K) = 2\overline \Phi(K)$, and
$\overline\Phi(K)\le\phi(K)/K$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:big-q-bound}
    \alpha G_K(\theta)
      \le\frac{q(r)}{K^2}\theta^2
      \le\frac8{(25/3)^2}\theta^2
      <.116\theta^2.
\end{equation}
This is smaller than \eqref{eq:near-binary-entropy-bound}.

Suppose now that $q(r)>8$.  Then
$t(r)=q(r)/(2r^2)>25/9.$
Factoring out the $j=1$ term in the series defining $Z_r$ and its
second moment gives
\[
    r^2-1
      \le\sum_{j\ge2}(j^2-1)e^{-(j^2-1)t(r)}
      <7.22\cdot10^{-4}.
\]
Here the $j=2$ term is retained and the remaining positive tail is
bounded geometrically.  In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-binary-delta}
    \delta:=r^2-1<7.3\cdot10^{-4}.
\end{equation}
Writing $X=S|X|$, where the sign $S$ is uniform on $\{\pm1\}$ and independent of $|X|$, we have
$\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[|X|-1\right]\le\delta/3$.  The geometric distribution maximizes entropy
among nonnegative integer-valued random variables with a fixed mean, and
therefore
\[
    H(\mu_r)
       \le\log2+g(\delta/3)
       <1.0033\log2,
    \qquad
    g(x):=(1+x)\log(1+x)-x\log x.
\]
The assumption $H(\mu_r) + \frac{q(r)}{d(K)} \log p(K) \geq 0$ implies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-binary-alpha-upper}
    \alpha\le1.0033\,\alpha_{\rm bin}(K).
\end{equation}

For $(X,Y)\sim\mu^{(2)}_{r,r,\theta}$, let $S=\mathrm{sign}(X)$ and
$T=\mathrm{sign}(Y)$.  Applying data processing to
\eqref{eq:Dr-relative-entropy}, and using
$\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[|X||Y|-1\right]\le r^2-1$, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sign-projection}
    D_r(\theta)
      \ge I_{\rm bin}\bigl([\theta-\delta(1-\theta)]_+\bigr).
\end{equation}
Indeed,
\[
    \mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[ST\right]
      =\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[XY\right]-\mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[ST(|X||Y|-1)\right]
      \ge\theta r^2-\delta
      =\theta-\delta(1-\theta).
\]
For $\theta\ge1/4$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:binary-information-loss}
    I_{\rm bin}(\theta-\delta(1-\theta))
       \ge.9955\,I_{\rm bin}(\theta).
\end{equation}
To see this, note that
\[
    I_{\rm bin}(\theta)
     -I_{\rm bin}(\theta-\delta(1-\theta))
     \le\delta(1-\theta)\mathrm{arctanh}\theta,
\]
while $I_{\rm bin}(\theta)\ge\theta^2/2$; the resulting ratio is at
most $.0045$.

For $\theta\le1/4$,
\eqref{eq:Gaussian-Hermite-refined},
\eqref{eq:near-binary-alpha-upper}, and
\eqref{eq:Gaussian-tail-two-sided} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-binary-center}
    \alpha G_K(\theta)<.045\theta^2
       <D_r(\theta).
\end{equation}
Here we used
\[
    \alpha_{\rm bin}(K)\frac{1-p(K)}{p(K)}
       \le\frac{\log2}{p(K)}<.7,
    \qquad
    \alpha_{\rm bin}(K)d(K)^2<10^{-12}.
\]

Now, if $\alpha\le.995\alpha_{\rm bin}(K),$
then \eqref{eq:ALS-global}--\eqref{eq:sign-projection} prove the main claim
for $\theta\ge1/4$, and \eqref{eq:near-binary-center} covers the
remaining interval.  

It thus remains to consider $\alpha>.995\alpha_{\rm bin}(K).$
Using
\[
    -\log p(K)\le\frac{1-p(K)}{p(K)} = \frac{2\overline{\Phi}(K)}{p(K)}
       \le\frac{2\phi(K)}{Kp(K)},
\]
we obtain
\[
    \frac{d(K)}{-\log p(K)}\ge K^2.
\]
Recall that stationarity gives $\alpha = q(r)/d(K)$, which yields 
\[
    q(r)>.995(\log2)K^2,
    \qquad
    t(r)>.239K^2.
\]
The defining series therefore yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:binary-exponential-radius}
    r^2-1\le4e^{-3t(r)}
       \le4e^{-.717K^2}.
\end{equation}

We first treat
\[
    \frac14\le\theta\le
    \theta_U:=1-\frac1{3K^2}.
\]
Let $P_K(\theta)=p^{(2)}(K,K,\theta)$. Integrating
\eqref{eq:energy_derivative}, using the two-sided Gaussian tail bound
\eqref{eq:Gaussian-tail-two-sided}, and evaluating the resulting
one-variable expressions on the intervals
\[
    [1/4,1/2],\quad[1/2,.8],\quad[.8,.95],\quad[.95,.98]
\]
gives
\[
    I_{\rm bin}(\theta)
     -1.0033\,\alpha_{\rm bin}(K)G_K(\theta)>.0315,
    \qquad \frac14\le\theta\le.98.
\]
For $.98\le\theta\le\theta_U$, let
$J_\pm=\mathbb{P}_{}\left[W>K,\ \pm W_\theta>K\right]$. Conditioning on
$(W+W_\theta,W-W_\theta)$ gives
\[
    J_+<.693\overline\Phi(K),\qquad J_-<10^{-3}\overline\Phi(K).
\]
Since
\[
    P_K(\theta)=p(K)^2+2(J_++J_-)-4\overline\Phi(K)^2,
\]
it follows that
$\alpha_{\rm bin}(K)G_K(\theta)<.482$, and hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:binary-middle-gap}
    I_{\rm bin}(\theta)
     -1.0033\,\alpha_{\rm bin}(K)G_K(\theta)>.0315,
    \qquad \frac14\le\theta\le\theta_U.
\end{equation}
All constants in the above computations are direct
outward-rounded evaluations, uniform for $K\ge25/3$.

The loss from replacing $\theta$ by
$\theta-\delta(1-\theta)$ in \eqref{eq:sign-projection} is at most
\[
    \delta(1-\theta)\mathrm{arctanh}\theta<.0045\log2 < .0032.
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:near-binary-alpha-upper} and
\eqref{eq:binary-middle-gap} prove the profile inequality on
$[1/4,\theta_U]$.

Finally, let $\theta=1-\varepsilon\in(\theta_U,1)$.  By \eqref{eq:binary-exponential-radius},
\[
    r^2-1<10^{-21},
    \qquad
    \mathbb{E}_{\unskip\space}\left[(Y-X)^2\right]=2r^2\varepsilon.
\]
Since $H(X)\le H(\mu_r)$, and since an integer-valued random variable
of second moment $2r^2\epsilon$ satisfies
\[
    H(Y-X)\le H(|Y-X|)+\mathbb{P}_{}\left[Y\ne X\right]\log2
       \le g(2r^2\epsilon)+2r^2\epsilon\log2,
\]
we obtain $H(\mu^{(2)}_{r,r,\theta})-H(\mu_r)\le2.5\varepsilon\log(e/\varepsilon).$
Concavity of $H(\mu_{r, r, \theta}^{(2)})$ (\cref{prop:F2 entropy derivatives}) therefore yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-binary-entropy-derivative}
    \partial_\theta H(\mu^{(2)}_{r,r,\theta})
       \ge-2.5\log\frac e\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
On the other hand, the derivative computation
\eqref{eq:energy_derivative} yields the following direct estimate.
Since $\alpha>.995\alpha_{\rm bin}(K)$,
$P_K(\theta)\le p(K)$, and
$-p(K)\log p(K)\le1-p(K)=2\overline\Phi(K)$,
\[
    \frac{\alpha}{P_K(\theta)}
       \ge\frac{.995\log2}{2\overline\Phi(K)}.
\]
The upper bound in \eqref{eq:Gaussian-tail-two-sided} therefore gives
\[
 \alpha\partial_\theta\log P_K(\theta)
 \ge
 \frac{.995\log2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,
 \frac{K}{\sqrt{\varepsilon(2-\varepsilon)}}\,
 \exp\left(-\frac{K^2\varepsilon}{2(2-\varepsilon)}\right)
 \left(1-\exp\left(-\frac{2K^2\theta}{1-\theta^2}\right)\right).
\]
Here $K^2\varepsilon\le1/3$, $K\ge25/3$, and $\theta \geq 0.98$, so $1-\exp(-2K^2\theta/(1-\theta^2)) \geq 1-e^{-100}$.  Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-binary-energy-derivative}
    \alpha\partial_\theta\log P_K(\theta)
       >.17K\varepsilon^{-1/2}
       >.16K\varepsilon^{-1/2}.
\end{equation}
At $\varepsilon=1/(3K^2)$ and $K=25/3$, the absolute value of the
right-hand side of \eqref{eq:near-binary-entropy-derivative} is less
than $15.85$, while the right-hand side of
\eqref{eq:near-binary-energy-derivative} is greater than $19.24$.
The comparison improves as $K$ grows or $\varepsilon$ decreases.
Thus $F_2'(\theta)>0$ on $(\theta_U,1)$.  Finally,
\[
    F_2(1)=H(\mu_r)+\alpha\log p(K)
       \le2(H(\mu_r)+\alpha\log p(K))=F_2(0),
\]
so the profile inequality $F_2(\theta) < F_2(0)$ follows on this last interval $\theta\in(\theta_U, 1)$.


Finally, we prove that $q(r)d(K) < 1$. If $q(r)\le8$, then by \eqref{eq:energy_derivative} and the computation directly following it, Taylor expansion at $\theta=0$ gives 
\[
    \alpha G_K(\theta)
       =\frac{q(r)d(K)}2\theta^2+O(\theta^4).
\]
Here, we have recalled $\alpha=q(r)/d(K)$, and then used symmetry of $G_K$ to eliminate the odd terms in the Taylor expansion. Hence, combining this expansion with \eqref{eq:big-q-bound} and taking $\theta \to 0$ gives $q(r)d(K)\le2\cdot0.116<1$. If $q(r)>8$, \eqref{eq:near-binary-center} similarly gives $q(r)d(K)\le2\cdot0.045<1$. This concludes the proof.
